title: Cell-specific RNA purification to study translatomes of mouse central nervous system
protocol: Wash surfaces, pipettes, tube racks, and pipette boxes before starting using Vikron, 1% bleach or RNase Away.
Keep everything cold.
Use pipette tips with filters.
Use DNase/RNase free 1.5 mL tubes, water and PBS.
Frequently change gloves to ensure they are clean.
Cull and decapitate the mouse following institutionally approved procedures.
Extract the brain and place it on a petri dish filled with RNase-free PBS under the dissection microscope.
Dissect the area of interest.
Cut the brain sagittally in two halves.
For each half, remove the thalamus and hippocampus.
When the striatum is exposed, detach it from the cortex using fine curved forceps.
Remove any remaining corpus callosum to clean the striatum.
Place the two dissected striata from a mouse into a Dounce homogenizer.
Homogenize samples at 2%–10% weight/volume with S-HB solution (1 mL for 30 mg of tissue).
First, homogenize with pestle “A” up and down 10 times.
Then, homogenize with pestle “B” for 15-20 times.
Keep the Dounce on ice between steps to prevent sample heating due to friction.
Transfer the homogenized sample to a 1.5 mL tube labeled with the sample ID.
Clean the Douncer with RNase-free water 3 times (5–10 strokes per pestle each time) between samples to avoid contamination.
Mix 1.5 ml collection tubes in advance as IP+HA, INPUT, and IP+BEADS for each sample.
Centrifuge homogenized samples at 4°C/10,000 g/10 min.
Transfer supernatant to the tube labeled IP+HA.
Take 5%–10% of the supernatant in the IP+HA tube and transfer it to the INPUT sample tube.
Add 400 μL of Lysis Buffer (1:100 β-mercaptoethanol:RLT buffer from RNeasy kit) to the supernatant.
Vortex for 10–30 s.
Freeze in liquid nitrogen or dry ice and store at −80°C.
Incubate IP samples with 5 μL of anti-HA antibody at a ratio of ∼1:200 vol/vol for 4 h at 4°C on a gentle spinner at 20 rpm.
Vortex the bead stock vigorously before use to homogenize the beads.
Add 200 μL of beads to IP+BEADS 1.5 mL tubes immediately after discarding storage buffer solution.
Incubate the beads with 800–1,000 μL of HB at 4°C on a gentle spinner for 10 min at 20 rpm.
Add the IP+HA sample to its corresponding IP+BEADS tube quickly.
Incubate 14–16 hours at 4°C on a gentle spinner at 20 rpm.
Place IP+BEADS tubes on the magnetic rack.
Discard the supernatant; the HA-ribosome/RNA complex will be bound to the beads.
Add 800 μL of high salt buffer to each sample immediately after removing the liquid.
Incubate at 4°C on a gentle spinner for 10 minutes.
Repeat the washes a total of 3 times.
Place tubes on the magnetic rack.
Discard the high salt buffer.
Add 350 μL of Lysis Buffer (1:100 β-mercaptoethanol:RLT buffer from RNeasy kit) to the beads of each sample immediately.
Vortex vigorously for 30 seconds (to break apart the antibody-bead-protein bond).
Freeze in liquid nitrogen or dry ice and store at −80°C.
Thaw INPUT and IP+BEADS samples on ice.
Place tubes with IP RNA on a magnetic rack to remove beads.
Use supernatant for RNA purification with RNeasy Micro QIAGEN kit.
Follow manufacturer’s instructions for the RNeasy Micro QIAGEN kit.
Store purified RNA at −80°C to avoid freeze/thaw cycles.
Set aside an aliquot of the sample before freezing for quality assessment.
Evaluate RNA integrity using the appropriate assay.
Assess RNA integrity to ensure it has not degraded during purification.
Use Agilent Bioanalyzer for RNA integrity assessment.
Check electrophoresis gel pictures for high RIN RNA quality examples.
Verify electropherograms for high RIN RNA quality examples.
Analyze poor quality, medium RIN RNA using electrophoresis gel pictures.
Examine poor quality, medium RIN RNA using electropherograms.
Evaluate bad quality, low RIN RNA with electrophoresis gel pictures.
Review bad quality, low RIN RNA with electropherograms.
Identify lower band and 18S and 28S ribosomal RNA bands in analysis.
Assess RNA integrity and abundance using an Agilent Bioanalyzer.
Check the cell specificity of the purified RNA if performing the protocol for the first time, investigating new brain regions, or using new CRE mouse lines.
Use qRT-PCR to assess RNA cell specificity.
Employ specific primers targeting RNAs enriched in the cell of interest.
Utilize primers targeting RNAs enriched in potential contaminating cells.
Transcribe complementary DNA (cDNA) from purified RNA using SuperScript™ IV Reverse Transcriptase following manufacturer instructions.
Reverse transcribe 20 ng of RNA.
Generate a 1:10 dilution of the cDNA stock once it is prepared.
Use 5 μL of the diluted cDNA for each qRT-PCR reaction.
Calculate cell-specific gene expression relative to the housekeeping Rplp0 based on their Ct values using the formula: 2-ΔCt (ΔCt = Ct (gene of interest) – Ct (housekeeping gene)).
Assess and present the expression of cell-specific genes relative to one or two housekeeping genes.
Present the expression as a ratio of enrichment in the IP vs its corresponding INPUT samples.
Conduct immunohistochemistry of the HA tag and a marker targeting the cell of interest, along with markers for other unrelated cell types, to assess cell specific RiboTag expression.
Perform a normality test (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) on replicates to check if they follow normal distributions.
Conduct a homogeneity of variance test (e.g., Brown-Forsythe test) between conditions.
Use repeated measures (RM) one-way ANOVA test if data are normally distributed and variances are homogeneous between conditions.
Use Friedman’s test if data are not normally distributed or variances are not homogeneous.
If statistical significance is shown, use post-hoc tests like Tukey’s or Dunn’s to assess differences between specific groups.
